title: Post-PRT SDI Path Selection

what_prt_proved: Canonical INT8 sidecar layout is valid representation artifact
/127 dequant fix restored correctness (Python round(f32/scale*127) requires C decode f32=int8*scale/127.0f)
3B and 7B layer0 correctness canaries pass after fix
Current GGML custom-op path is slower than native Q4_K_M in narrow 3B c=4 n=8 smoke (PRT ~36% slower)
prt_lesson.core_lesson: PRT is a valid representation/correctness artifact, not the active speed path

option_1_specbenchcpu.question: Can we get practical CPU speedups by routing code-like prompts to speculative decoding?

option_2_sdi_router.question: Can we make a real system-level SDI stack using routing, preloading, small/large model selection, speculative mode, context routing, and memory compression?

option_3_context_memory.question: Can we reduce compute waste by improving context/memory handling instead of kernel math?

option_4_prt_v3_design.question: Should PRT continue as design branch only, not implementation?

option_5_local_inference_productization.question: Can we package current local inference stack into something useful sooner?

1_recommended.why: Lowest risk path to new concrete win; prior code speedup evidence; fits router architecture; creates real selectable-diversity inference stack
1_recommended.first_concrete_phase: 26B: SpecBenchCPU verify + 1 code-prompt timing smoke + SDI routing policy design
success_criteria: Code-prompt speculative decoding shows measurable speedup (no claim, just observe)
Router can route to speculative path based on prompt classification
risks: SpecBenchCPU may regress on current branch (low risk)
Speedup may be smaller than prior runs
Router SDI policy layer adds complexity

2_second_best.why: VaultBrain already completed; MemoryOS is documented SDI pillar; good product story; reasonable engineering effort
2_second_best.first_concrete_phase: 26B/27: Audit VaultBrain/ClawVault integration + design context compression for repetitive patterns
success_criteria: At least one compute-saving mechanism identified
risks: May overlap with existing ClawVault work
Hard to measure without concrete demo workload

3_parked.why: High complexity, no clear demo path, currently the slowest path. Revisit only after Option 1 produces a concrete win and someone has a specific native backend hypothesis.

recommended_next_phase.title: SpecBenchCPU Router Revalidation
scope: Run SpecBenchCPU on current branch — verify speculative decoding correctness still passes
One small code-prompt timing smoke (1 native run, 1 speculative run, no repeat)
Document current router architecture + SDI mode design proposal
Do NOT make speedup claims yet
recommended_next_phase.purpose: Confirm speculative decoding path is still good, then design SDI routing layer on top of it

what_not_to_do_next: More PRT speed work on current custom-op path
